## class Caligrafy\Controller

Parent Class that defines the properties and methods of a controller

Its 17 public methods have a page of their own: [Caligrafy\Controller](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/wiki/API-Controller).

<a name="pagecontroller"></a>
## class Caligrafy\PageController

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class PageController extends Controller
```

Source: [framework/core/PageController.php:25](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/PageController.php#L25)

Class PageController
Route::page('/books/{id}', 'Books/show', ['data' =&gt; ['book' =&gt; 'get_book']]) renders a view through this controller:
1. access: 'signedIn' =&gt; true sends visitors to /login; 'level' =&gt; N also sends people below level N to /notAuthorized (Auth::guard on Context::$levelAttribute)
2. data: each 'data' entry calls a read-only capability as the person who opens the page ($this-&gt;call(): the same rules as REST and MCP), with the query string and the route variables as inputs (the route variables win), or with the inputs it lists (['book' =&gt; ['get_book', ['id' =&gt; 3]]]). A refusal becomes the page's answer: a visitor is sent to sign in; otherwise 403 (error 1006) or 404 (error 1005), or the 'notFound' view (route variables, 'with', 'message', who opens it) with a 404 status
3. the view gets the route variables, 'with' values, the data, 'authorized' and 'user' (id, username, level) - never the query string
Pages never read models: capabilities do, so a page, REST and AI agents follow the same rules.

### Constants

+ `RESERVED = array('authorized', 'user')`

#### `->render()`

```php

```

**Parameters**

+ `$view` `string`: the view, as for view(): 'Books/show'
+ `$options` `array`, default `array()`: 'signedIn' (bool), 'level' (int), 'data' (array name =&gt; read-only capability or [capability, inputs]), 'with' (array of fixed view data), 'notFound' (a view for 404s); 2.20.0: 'visitorsOnly' (a path: signed-in people go there), 'comeBack' (bool: visitors come back here after signing in), 'query' (names of the query string the view gets, as strings, '' when absent)

<a name="view-display"></a>
#### `View::display()`

```php
public static function display($path, array $data = array())
```

Prints a Pug file (2.19.0). A view already compiled and up to date runs through Phug's Optimizer, which includes
the compiled PHP without building Phug's compiler (3 classes instead of about 100); a view to compile, or a
project that customized Phug at run time (its renderer already built), goes through Phug's renderer as before.

**Parameters**

+ `$path`
+ `$data` `array`, default `array()`

Source: [framework/core/View.php:49](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/View.php#L49)

<a name="view-cache"></a>
#### `View::cache()`

```php
public static function cache()
```

Compiled templates are kept between requests: a view is compiled to PHP once, then again only when it or a file
it includes or extends changes. On by default; VIEW_CACHE=false compiles every view on every request. A project
that sets Phug's cache_dir itself keeps its own. Returns the folder used, or null (no cache). Also sets Phug's
debug mode from APP_DEBUG.

Source: [framework/core/View.php:91](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/View.php#L91)

<a name="view-cachefolder"></a>
#### `View::cacheFolder()`

```php
public static function cacheFolder()
```

A folder of the system's temporary directory for this project and this system user only (compiled templates are
PHP that runs): created private (0700), refused when someone else owns it or it cannot be written. Views compiled
in debug mode are kept apart (the cache does not know the options a view was compiled with).

Source: [framework/core/View.php:109](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/View.php#L109)

<a name="designs"></a>
## class Caligrafy\Designs

```php
namespace Caligrafy;

class Designs
```

Source: [framework/core/Designs.php:21](https://github.com/caligrafy/caligrafy-quill/blob/v2.25.0/framework/core/Designs.php#L21)

Class Designs
A style is a DESIGN.md and the override stylesheet written from it, public/css/designs/&lt;name&gt;.css. DESIGN.md files
are looked up in this order, the first one wins on a name clash:

```
application/design/<name>/                the project's own styles
framework/design/local/<name>/            styles added to Caligrafy itself
framework/design/vendor/<vendor>/<name>/  collections copied from elsewhere (awesome-design-md...), by vendor name
```

The layout loads that stylesheet after the Caligrafy stylesheets when DESIGN_STYLE names it; an empty DESIGN_STYLE,
an unknown name or a style without its stylesheet keeps Caligrafy's own look.

### Constants

+ `VENDOR = 'framework/design/vendor'`
+ `LOCAL = 'framework/design/local'`
+ `APPLICATION = 'application/design'`
+ `STYLESHEETS = 'public/css/designs'`
